messages:
maya: quick flag — saw a p99 jump on the 13B quant pipeline after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. p95 stable but p99 slices up ~2.5x for some long-history chats.

sandeep: can you paste the trace id / example payload? is this correlated with seq_len > 1024?

maya: trace 1765432100-TH. Example: user convo with 3200 total tokens (prefix 2400 + request 800). observed spike when microbatch merged two tall requests.

eli: looked at profiler. root cause looks like kernel fallback: for attention patterns > 2048 we hit the slow fp32_attention kernel because the new fused-kv kernel refuses due to contiguity check. fallback adds ~180ms on cold kv cache.

kat: so this is a combo: kernel selection + microbatch merge -> huge KV cache miss and then expensive kernel + re-populate KV?

eli: exactly. Also the KV cache trim path currently runs async but blocks the next token path for the microbatch owner; that path has a lock contention bug.

maya: ops impact: p99 for this route moved from ~380ms to ~950ms under mixed traffic. We need a short-term mitigation to protect tail SLOs before kernel fix lands.

sandeep: immediate mitigations to consider: 1) server-side max_tokens cap for responses, 2) refuse merging microbatches that would create seq_len > 2300, 3) apply per-request timeout (hard cap) to avoid infinite tail blowups. Thoughts?

kat: I like (2) + (1) as quick wins. If we cap response tokens to 512 for that model then most long-history chats still serve, and heavy ones get truncated. We should make cap configurable per-model.

eli: adding a guard in microbatcher is low-risk: microbatcher currently has param max_combined_tokens. set to 2300 for 13B until kernel updated. also add metric "microbatch_reject_long_combo".

maya: will adding that kill throughput badly? we care about throughput/latency tradeoff.

eli: throughput will dip slightly (fewer merged requests), but p99 will improve dramatically for affected routes. We can measure with canary.

sandeep: propose rollout plan:
- step 1: server config change, model=redwood-13b-q4, max_combined_tokens=2300 (config flag)
- step 2: server-side response cap: max_response_tokens=512 for same model, with client-level override allowed only for enterprise tenants (opt-in).
- step 3: short circuit expensive kernel fallback by forcing quantized fused-kv kernel on sequences up to 4096 if memory safe (fast path).

kat: for step 2, we should also send a small system token back to clients explaining truncation so apps can surface a retry link. e.g. 
```
{"warning":"response_truncated","reason":"tail_safety","max_tokens":512}
```

maya: agree. Also set a per-request hard timeout of 6s for token streaming (server-side). If exceeded, emit telemetry and return partial streaming chunk + truncation warning.

ops-bot: Incident detection rule updated: "13B_tail_latency_regression" -> alert when p99 > 700ms for route redwood-13b-q4 for 3m. (configured by sandeep) :white_check_mark:

eli: I'll push the microbatcher guard as a config toggle to canary tonight. also adding the metric so we can graph the rejections.

maya: I'll coordinate a canary and collect p50/p95/p99. let's target 2% traffic canary and monitor for 30m.

sandeep: long-term: we need better kernel selection heuristics that consider expected KV cache warmness and microbatch merge cost. propose an experiment to add a cost model: expected_kernel_time = f(seq_len, cache_hit_rate, batch_size). then choose kernel minimizing expected_tail.

kat: yes — and tie that to routing: if predicted_tail > SLO, route to smaller dedicated GPU with quantized-kernel pinned (higher cost but lower tail).

eli: filed GH PR with microbatch guard: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821 (draft). will add unit tests for config edge cases.

maya: thanks. after canary, if p99 drops back near baseline we keep changes and schedule kernel patch next sprint. If not, roll back.

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary (redwood-13b-q4) -> rollout_id=cb-176543. Monitoring endpoints: /metrics/canary/cb-176543

sandeep: leaving this thread open for telemetry. please paste canary metrics here once we have 30m. :eyes:
